answer_text:
Let

\[
A_n(x)=1+\sin^2 x+\sin^2(2x)+\cdots+\sin^2(nx)
=1+\sum_{k=1}^n \sin^2(kx).
\]

For fixed \(n\), as \(x\to 0\),

\[
\sin(kx)=kx+O(x^3),
\]

so

\[
\sin^2(kx)=k^2x^2+O(x^4).
\]

Therefore,

\[
A_n(x)=1+x^2\sum_{k=1}^n k^2+O(x^4).
\]

Let

\[
c_n=\sum_{k=1}^n k^2.
\]

Then

\[
\ln A_n(x)=\ln\left(1+c_nx^2+O(x^4)\right)
= c_nx^2+O(x^4).
\]

Hence

\[
\lim_{x\to 0} A_n(x)^{\frac{1}{n^3x^2}}
=
\exp\left(\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\ln A_n(x)}{n^3x^2}\right)
=
\exp\left(\frac{c_n}{n^3}\right).
\]

Now

\[
c_n=\sum_{k=1}^n k^2=\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{c_n}{n^3}
=
\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6n^3}
\to \frac{1}{3}
\qquad (n\to\infty).
\]

Therefore,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\lim_{x\to 0} A_n(x)^{\frac{1}{n^3x^2}}\right)
=
\exp\left(\frac{1}{3}\right).
\]

\[
\boxed{e^{1/3}}
\]
